name: Comply With A Failing Policy (Missing Output Quality Promise)

checks.check: Before editing any file, the agent identifies the failing policy's TYPE as DataQualityCompliance (namespace nextdata, name require-output-quality) by reading the nxd describe output / policy status, rather than jumping straight to spec edits.

The agent distinguishes the existing input expectation (the Soda check attached to source_aligned_input via .expectation(quality(soda, ...))) from the MISSING output promise, and correctly states the fix belongs on the OUTPUT port (storage(...).promise(quality(...))), not on the input.

The agent's fix ADDS an enforced data-quality promise (Great Expectations or Soda) to the snowflake output port via storage(...).promise(quality(gx|soda, "contracts/...")), and authors/declares the corresponding contract file. It does NOT merely add a schema-only .promise(model) and does NOT disable, deactivate, weaken the consequence to WARN, or delete the policy to make it 'pass'.

Any activate/verify command the agent gives uses the flag shape from nxd activate policy --help (e.g. --name, --policy DataQualityCompliance, --validation-url, --output-ports at-least-one, --filter, --consequence, --promise-enforced, --env) and does NOT invent flags that are absent from the help output.

The final answer includes the exact verify commands needed to prove compliance after the fix (at minimum re-running nxd describe data-product customer-orders-curated --env demo to confirm policy STATUS is no longer FAILED, and/or nxd ls policies / re-running the data product so the promise executes), with concrete data-product name and env, not vague guidance.
